bib.title: Visual Planning: Let's Think Only with Images

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "VisualPlanning: Let's Think Only with Images", Yi Xu*, Chengzu Li*, Han Zhou* (equal), Xingchen Wan, Caiqi Zhang, Anna Korhonen, Ivan Vulić (Cambridge LTL, Google). ICLR 2026 (arXiv 2505.11409v3, 20 Feb 2026). Code: github.com/yix8/VisualPlanning.

COVERAGE: 102,712 of 102,712 chars, all 34 pages. The reference list was skimmed. Pages 33-34 (the rest of the prompt templates in Appendix G) were skimmed, not read closely. Main text, limitations, all appendix tables and figure captions were read.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: VPRL (the two-stage GRPO visual planner on LVM-7B) beats every baseline on all three navigation tasks. It averages 80.6% EM against 53.6% for the text SFT baseline, a gap of 27 points.
  number: 80.6 vs 53.6 EM avg; PR 84.9 vs 69.9
  setup: LVM-7B, trained only on images/video and no text. Baseline is Qwen2.5-VL-7B SFT, trained on the same data. Tasks are FrozenLake, Maze and MiniBehavior, synthetic grids. Single model per cell, no seeds or error bars reported. Evaluation starts from the initial state v0 only.
  quote: "VPRL † (ours)/ctre /ctre91.6 93.2 74.5 77.6 75.8 83.8 80.6 84.9" and "- SFT† /fnt+/ctre /fnt68.6 84.4 60.9 70.3 31.3 56.1 53.6 69.9"
  where: Table 1, p6

- claim: Per task, VPRL reaches EM of 91.6 (FrozenLake), 74.5 (Maze) and 75.8 (MiniBehavior). Plain supervised visual planning (VPFT) reaches 75.4, 59.0 and 33.8, so VPFT is only roughly on par with text SFT.
  number: 91.6 / 74.5 / 75.8 vs 75.4 / 59.0 / 33.8
  setup: as above. VPRL beats VPFT by over 20% on average.
  quote: "VPFT† (ours)/ctre /ctre75.4 79.5 59.0 64.0 33.8 52.2 56.1 65.2"; "outperforming VPFT by over 20% on average"
  where: Table 1 and p7

- claim: Closed models are weak on these tasks. Gemini 2.5 Pro (think) averages 43.7 EM and Gemini 2.0 Flash CoT 12.8 EM.
  number: 43.7 / 12.8 avg EM (Maze 21.5 for 2.5 Pro)
  setup: text+image in, text out, prompted only. Qwen2.5-VL-7B Direct gets 0.7 avg EM and CoT 3.7.
  quote: "Gemini 2.5 Pro (think)/fnt+/ctre /fnt72.0 85.0 21.5 35.5 37.6 59.9 43.7 60.1"
  where: Table 1

- claim: Text planners degrade sharply as grids grow, while visual planners decline more slowly. On FrozenLake, Gemini 2.5 Pro EM falls from 98.0% (3x3) to 38.8% (6x6). VPRL falls from 97.6% to 82.4%.
  number: 98.0 -> 38.8 vs 97.6 -> 82.4
  setup: FrozenLake, grid sizes 3 to 6, 250 test environments per size.
  quote: "Gemini 2.5 Pro's EM score drops sharply from 98.0% to 38.8%... EM remaining at 97.6% on 3×3 grids and still achieving 82.4% on 6×6"
  where: p7, Fig 5. Per-size table is Table 7 (VPFT 92.0 -> 58.0).

- claim: RL in text does not help here. GRPO on Qwen2.5-VL-7B text planning stays below the SFT baseline. The authors blame a modality gap, in grounding the image into text, as the cause.
  number: 54.4 and 60.1 EM vs SFT 68.6
  setup: FrozenLake, same progress reward as VPRL (54.4) or the PR metric as reward (60.1). Group size 8, 10 epochs.
  quote: "Table 2 shows that when using progress reward as in VPRL or directly using the Progress Rate metric as the outcome reward, none of the variants surpasses the SFT baseline."
  where: Table 2, p7. Full results in Table 7, p21.

- claim: Verbalised layouts are often wrong. Text-planner coordinate descriptions mismatch the ground truth 25.7% of the time and ASCII descriptions 22.3%. Adding coordinate or ASCII descriptions before the answer gives small EM gains (68.6 -> 74.4 / 73.1) but lower PR.
  number: 25.7% / 22.3%
  setup: FrozenLake text SFT variants. The two figures come from the error analysis, which the paper does not tie to a specific model size.
  quote: "with 25.7% of generated coordinate-based layout descriptions and 22.3% of generated ASCII-based representations being mismatched with ground-truth layouts"
  where: p8

- claim: Stage 1 (random-walk policy initialisation) gives no planning skill but is needed for RL. After Stage 1 alone, EM is near random. Without it, VPFT's entropy collapses and GRPO advantages go to zero.
  number: Stage 1 EM 11.1 / 9.6 / 0.5 vs Stage 2 91.6 / 74.5 / 75.8
  setup: LVM-7B. Entropy comparison on FrozenLake (Fig 6). VPFT* (Stage 1 then VPFT) scores lower than VPFT: 6x6 EM 33.2 vs 58.0.
  quote: "VPRL Stage 1 11.1 27.2 9.6 22.7 0.5 14.2" / "VPRL Stage 2 91.6 93.2 74.5 77.6 75.8 83.8"
  where: Table 10 p27; Table 8 p22; Fig 6 p9

- claim: VPRL cuts invalid-action failures. Share of failed trajectories containing at least one invalid action: VPRL 36.9 / 25.1 / 29.6 vs VPFT 60.6 / 73.7 / 78.3.
  number: see claim
  setup: the three tasks (FrozenLake, Maze, MiniBehavior).
  quote: "FROZENLAKE36.960.6 / MAZE25.173.7 / MINIBEHAVIOR29.678.3"
  where: Table 6, p20. The main text says "at least 24%" reduction, in the intro of Sec 4.

- claim: OOD generalisation to larger grids is weak in absolute terms. VPRL is better than VPFT, but it is low everywhere.
  number: FrozenLake 7x7 EM 20.4 vs 9.6; Maze 7x7 10.0 vs 9.2; MiniBehavior 9x9 0.4 vs 0.0
  setup: trained on smaller grids, 250 OOD samples per task. Also run qualitatively with masked inputs (Fig 12).
  quote: "VPFT 9.6 15.3 9.2 17.8 0.0 5.8 / VPRL 20.4 31.2 10.0 21.6 0.4 14.7"
  where: Table 9, p22

- claim: Visual planning costs more tokens than text CoT. Average 1082.5 tokens for LVM-7B, roughly 3x Qwen CoT (298.3) and 6x Gemini 2.0 Flash CoT (171.2). Gemini 2.5 Pro thinking averages 1178.6.
  number: 1082.5 vs 298.3 / 171.2 / 1178.6
  setup: average generated tokens per task, across three tasks.
  quote: "the token cost of our visual planner is roughly 3 times that of Qwen 2.5-VL-Instruct-7B with CoT and around 6 times that of Gemini 2.0 Flash with CoT"
  where: Table 12 and p32

- claim: Generated image quality is not the bottleneck. Feeding ground-truth images instead of self-generated ones at inference changes little. The artifacts come from the VQGAN tokenizer, not the planner.
  number: EM 91.6 (self-generated) vs 92.1 (ground-truth)
  setup: VPRL on FrozenLake.
  quote: "VPRL - (w/ self-generated images) ... 91.6 ... (w/ ground-truth images) ... 92.1"
  where: Table 11, p31

- claim: Reward design is simple. Progress reward is +1 for a valid move that reduces BFS distance to the goal, 0 for a valid non-progressing move, and -5 for an invalid move.
  number: 1 / 0 / -5
  quote: "we set αopt = 1, αnopt = 0, and αinv =−5"
  where: Eq. 4, p5

LIMITS
- Authors concede (App. D):
  - Only LVM-7B was used, because it is the only size available. Native multimodal generators were excluded.
  - Image generation adds inference overhead.
  - The dynamics interpreter is rule-based and pixel-wise (IoU/MSE on grayscale grid cells). Harder visual structures are untested. The authors name segmentation, contour detection, a Gemini-style judge or a learned reward model as future options.
  - Failures remain: agents disappearing, teleporting or walking through walls (Fig 13-14).
- Not shown (my reading):
  - Only small synthetic grid navigation. Real images, robotics and non-grid tasks are not tested.
  - The progress estimator is BFS with privileged access to the environment, so the RL reward is not learned.
  - The comparison is a visual planner against fine-tuned text VLMs. The planner was run on LVM-7B only, which has no text pretraining.
  - No seeds or confidence intervals.
  - OOD EM is low, at most 20.4%.
  - Text RL was reward-limited by the authors' own account. Their reward could not tell trajectory orderings apart, and this was one setup.
  - MiniBehavior grids were 7x7 and 8x8 only, with duplicated layouts.
  - Gemini 2.5 Pro was prompted, not trained.
  - Models are from 2025 (Gemini 2.0/2.5, Qwen2.5-VL); later models may differ.
- Paper's framing: visual planning is a "supplement" to language reasoning, not a replacement. Its conclusion says visual representations give "performance comparable to text-based planning" (VPFT), and the gains come from RL.

BUILDS ON: LVM, Bai et al. 2024 (backbone; VQGAN tokenizer, 256 tokens per image); GRPO, Shao et al. 2024 and DeepSeek-R1, Guo et al. 2025a; "SFT memorizes, RL generalizes", Chu et al. 2025; Dual Coding Theory, Paivio 1991; Moulton & Kosslyn 2009; MVoT, Li et al. 2025; Visual Sketchpad, Hu et al. 2024; environments FrozenLake (VSP, Wu et al. 2024b), Maze (Ivanitskiy et al. 2023), Mini-BEHAVIOR (Jin et al. 2023); Qwen2.5-VL (Bai et al. 2025); world models (Ha & Schmidhuber 2018; Hafner et al. 2019; Genie 3, Ball et al. 2025); Qiu et al. 2025 (dynamics models); LoRA (Hu et al. 2022); TRL (von Werra et al. 2020).

CODE: none in the paper beyond the pseudo-formulas below.
- Policy-init loss (Eq. 2): L_VPFT(θ) = −E[log π_θ(ṽ_{i+1} | v_≤i)], with the target sampled randomly from all valid next states, p4.
- Group advantage: A(k) = (r(k) − mean{r}) / std{r}.
- Hyperparameters (Table 5): LoRA; Stage 1 10 epochs, lr 1.5e-4; Stage 2 10 epochs, lr 5e-5, group size 10, KL β=0.001; 8xA100.

FIGURES (captions only; figures not rendered or viewed)
- Fig 1, p2: compares direct prompting, multimodal CoT and Visual Planning (pure image trajectory). Best single picture of the paradigm.
- Fig 2, p4: VPRL pipeline. Generate G candidate next images, parse the action with the dynamics interpreter, score optimal / non-optimal / invalid, GRPO update.
- Fig 3, p7: example traces for optimal, non-optimal and invalid actions on the three tasks.
- Fig 4, p8: FrozenLake example. Gemini 2.5 Pro spends 7000+ thinking tokens and concludes no path exists. VPRL goes around the obstacle where VPFT gets stuck.
- Fig 5, p9: accuracy vs grid size. Text methods drop faster than visual ones.
- Fig 6, p9: entropy vs invalid ratio, VPFT vs VPRL Stage 1. Explains why Stage 1 is needed.
- Figs 13-15, pp28-30: success and failure traces. Fig 16, p31: tokenizer artifact reconstruction.

PROBLEMS: Extraction had table columns concatenated (e.g. "91.6 93.2 74.5...") and glyph artifacts ("Vuli´c", "/fnt", "/ctre" for text/image icons). I decoded Table 1's columns as FrozenLake EM/PR, Maze EM/PR, MiniBehavior EM/PR, Avg EM/PR from the header, and the "27%" claim checks out (80.6 - 53.6 = 27.0). Figures were not viewed. No embedded instructions found in the PDF text.
